subject: Re: Prepay structure & payment term exceptions for Acme Health
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Prepay structure & payment term exceptions for Acme Health

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was pleased with the latency profiles and the model governance features. Procurement here is evaluating the commercial structure. A couple of asks from our side before we proceed to legal:

- We are evaluating a multi-year prepay (looking at 2–3 years) and want to understand how term discounts and ramp schedules would be structured.
- Our standard is Net30, but for long-term prepay we may be able to take Net60/Net90 for final invoices. Can Redwood make a payment-terms exception tied to prepay size or milestone completion?

Specifically: would Redwood consider partial upfront + milestone-linked payments, and conditionally extend Net60 for any invoice that is not upfront? We are sensitive to cashflow but can commit to higher prepay if we get a steeper term discount.

Can you share an example structure and a draft quote we can circulate with procurement?

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of IT Procurement
Acme Health
elena.rossi@acmehealth.com
[attachment: Acme_RFP_Notes.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-22T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & payment term exceptions for Acme Health

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. We can be flexible on term and payment structure for strategic, multi-year prepay commitments. Below are two practical options we typically offer; we can tweak numbers once we have an expected ARR/commit amount.

Option A — 3yr annual prepay (preferred for deepest discount)
- Commitment: Prepay annually at start of each year for 3 years
- Discount: 25% off list for a 3yr annual prepay (paid at each year start)
- Payment terms: Upfront payments are due on signing each year; we can extend the final 25% tranche per year to Net60 if customer requests and if the upfront for that year >= 50% of that year’s invoice.

Option B — 2yr blended prepay (mid discount, more flexible)
- Commitment: 2-year term with 50% upfront on signing, 25% on milestone (prod launch), 25% invoiced Net60
- Discount: 18% off list across term

Milestone / Ramp schedule (example)
- Milestone 1: Integration complete and test tokens: 20% of year amount
- Milestone 2: Production launch (SLA enabled): 30% of year amount
- Remaining invoiced as per payment term (Net60)

Finance note on exceptions
- For Net60/Net90 exceptions we generally: 1) require a minimum prepay threshold ($250k–$500k depending on term) OR 2) apply a small deferred-payment fee (1–2%) if customer requires Net90.

I’m attaching a first-pass quote (v2) that maps the 3yr and 2yr examples to ACME sizing we discussed. Monica from Sales Ops will follow with a clean quote and SOW including milestone definitions. Vivek (finance) is looped for payment-term approval — Monica, can you prepare the official quote for legal/procurement?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[attachment: RW-Quote-ACME-3yr-Prepay-v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME - Updated quote & milestone SOW (per Ben)

Thanks Ben — attached is an updated quote and a draft SOW that spells out the milestone acceptance criteria and the ramp schedule. Highlights:

- Pricing: 3yr annual prepay (25% discount) and 2yr blended prepay (18% discount) options included on pages 2–3.
- Billing: Invoice schedule tied to milestones; we show the 50/25/25 split for the 2yr option.
- Payment terms: We left terms as Net30 on the line items but included a payment-terms exception row for Net60 on final invoices when upfront payment >= 50% of year spend, and an option to request Net90 with a 1.5% deferred-payment fee.
- Next steps: If you confirm which option, we’ll generate a DocuSign packet with the selected schedule and include standard SLAs.

Attachments: SOW_Milestones.xlsx (spreadsheet with milestone text), RW-Quote-ACME-3yr-Prepay-v2.pdf (pricing)

Monica Patel
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
[attachment: SOW_Milestones.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-24T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ACME - Updated quote & milestone SOW (per Ben)

Looping in Finance approval notes — we can approve a Net60 exception for the final invoice if the following conditions are met:

1) Total prepay commitment >= $500k for the initial year OR cumulative prepay across term >= $1.2M.
2) Milestone acceptance criteria must be unambiguous and signed off by Acme technical lead (SOW will include sign-off checklist).
3) For Net90 requests we require either an incremental 1.5% deferred-payment fee or a letter of credit; otherwise limit to Net60.
4) Redwood reserves the right to require upfront payment for any optional add-ons (e.g., extra Dedicated capacity).

I’ve attached a short internal memo confirming the above and recommending that Sales obtain procurement agreement on milestone sign-off language before DocuSign. Once procurement confirms, we can waive the standard Net30 and use Net60 for the final tranche.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
[attachment: Finance_Approval_Memo.pdf (PDF)]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - Updated quote & milestone SOW (per Ben)

Ben / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping finance. Procurement reviewed the options with our CFO and counter-proposals below:

- Term: We would prefer a 2-year commitment rather than 3 years (primary driver: budget uncertainty across FY27).
- Payment structure: 40% upfront on signing, 30% on production launch milestone (as defined in SOW), and 30% final invoice. We can accept Net90 on the final invoice if the deferred-payment fee is 1% (we prefer flexibility over the extra cost).
- Ramp: We’d like the ramp to be frontloaded so Year 1 provides 60% of reserved capacity, Year 2 at 40% (this helps our internal adoption plan).

If Redwood can confirm the 2-year discount at 17% (to bridge to the 2yr mid-discount) and accept the 40/30/30 schedule with final invoice Net90 at 1%, we can move to signature this week.

Please provide an updated quote and DocuSign packet reflecting those changes so procurement can sign.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of IT Procurement
Acme Health
elena.rossi@acmehealth.com
[Procurement contact: procurement@acmehealth.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - Updated quote & milestone SOW (per Ben)

Elena — appreciate the clear counter. We can accommodate your request with the following confirmed terms:

- Term: 2-year commitment
- Discount: 17% off list across the 2-year term (as requested)
- Payment schedule: 40% upfront on signing, 30% on production launch (Milestone 2), 30% final invoice. Final invoice payment term: Net90 with a 1.0% deferred-payment fee.
- Ramp: Year 1 capacity 60%, Year 2 capacity 40% (we’ll add quota caps in the SOW and allow limited burst credits).
- Conditions: Net90 approval contingent on signed milestone acceptance criteria in SOW and total contract value >= $650k. If the contract value is below that threshold, Finance will revert to Net60.

Next steps: Monica will update the quote and SOW to reflect these confirmed numbers and push a DocuSign packet. Once Procurement signs, Legal will review standard redlines (we expect minimal changes).

Thanks — ready to proceed once you confirm the contract value and we push DocuSign.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
